transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Jenna Liu, Max Chen (Redwood); Marcus Reed, Priya Nair, Owen Park, Leah Kim (Aurora Tech)
Recording id: ff-20260305-aurora-console-01

Summary: Quick Console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated, wants token-level cost attribution, per-route SLOs, and audit logs/KMS for security. Agreed to share benchmarks and schedule POC kickoff if sizing aligns.

Topics: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, routing policies, caching & batching impact on cost, security (KMS, SOC2), next steps for POC

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm samir, account lead for aurora, and with me is jenna on the se side and max on cs.
[00:15] Marcus: hey, marcus here, vp eng at aurora. excited to see the console stuff - we want a clear view of cost per product route.
[00:22] Jenna: awesome, i'll share my screen in a sec, this is gonna be a live console walkthrough - sorry if the resolution is a bit choppy on your end.
[00:35] Owen: we mainly care about latency 95 and cost per call. our platform has dozens of routes, some are embedding heavy and some are short generation.
[00:45] Jenna: got it. i'm opening the Usage Analytics tab - first thing you'll see is a high level cost/time breakdown by model and route. you can filter by time window, region, and by customer tags.
[01:10] Jenna: (screen) so this top chart is token spend over time, below is avg p99 latency and error rate. on the right we have per-route cost share - notice route names can be aliased to your internal names, we can ingest tags from your API calls.
[01:40] Priya: can you show per-route token breakdown? we need to bill internal teams for usage.
[01:48] Jenna: yep - click into a route, here's 'search-embed-v2' - you get tokens in, tokens out, model used, and an estimated cost column. the cost uses your selected pricing profile - for Hosted it's per-token unit cost, for Dedicated it's a proportionalized cost based on reserved capacity and measured usage.
[02:25] Marcus: that proportionalized Dedicated calc - is that based on committed GPU hours or on actual token throughput?
[02:33] Jenna: good question - for Dedicated we compute an effective per-token cost using committed instance hours plus burst usage; the console shows both the amortized committed cost and the marginal cost for burst. there was a tiny typo in older docs calling it 'amortized GPU costs' but functionally it's committed-hours based.
[02:55] Owen: how does batching and kv cache influence those numbers? our embeddings pipeline could benefit from batching but sensitive about latency for search.
[03:05] Jenna: batching and KV cache are surfaced in the Optimize suggestions tab - you'll see an estimated percent cost savings if you enable prefix caching or increase batch windows. for example on this route enabling 50ms batching gave a modeled 18% token cost reduction and negligible p95 increase in our sim.
[03:30] Samir: we should point out real-world results vary, we recommend a small benchmark run which jenna will run with your traffic trace.
[03:40] Jenna: yes i can run a 24hr sim - i have a benchmark spreadsheet i'll share. (links: Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.link/benchmarks/aurora-03)
[03:55] Priya: about security - we need KMS integration, SSO, and zone-restricted logging.
[04:05] Max: we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; Hosted also can integrate with cloud KMS for key wrapping. audit logs with redaction and configurable retention are available - i'll drop the SOC2 and audit docs after.
[04:25] Leah: for procurement, can you send contract terms and SLAs?
[04:30] Samir: yes i'll include our SLA summary and contract template.
[04:35] Jenna: back to the console, another useful view is the per-route token heatmap - you can see spikes and drill to traces. here's a sample where a spike correlated with a model fallback to a larger model after an error. the console flags fallbacks so you can attribute cost to retries or rollouts.
[05:05] Marcus: can you split cost by model family? we need to see how much is going to open-source quantized variants vs large hosted models.
[05:12] Jenna: absolutely, there's a model-level breakdown. you can group by model version and see token counts and cost. also we keep an inventory of model variants and a compatibility matrix if you want to auto-fallback to cheaper quantized variants.
[05:35] Owen: what about per-caller or per-team billing?
[05:40] Jenna: you can tag requests with 'team' or 'product' and then the console aggregates cost by tag. we also export CSVs and have an API to pull granular usage for your internal billing system.
[05:55] Marcus: latency SLOs - can we set alerts on p95 for specific routes?
[06:02] Jenna: yes per-route SLOs and alerts - you can create an alert policy that triggers if p95 > X ms for Y minutes. alerts integrate with Slack/pagerduty.
[06:15] Max: also note in Dedicated we can reserve lower-latency hardware and guarantee throughput under SLA.
[06:25] Priya: can you show the route TV dashboard for an example route?
[06:30] Jenna: sure - this is 'chat-widget' - shows request rate, latency percentiles, token breakdown, top prompts by token usage, and cost per 1000 requests. top-right you can toggle model variants and see instantaneous cost delta.
[06:55] Jenna: small transcription hiccup: sometimes our auto captions read KV as 'k v' in the transcript, so apologies for weirdness.
[07:05] Owen: about retention - logs for 13 months is ok, we need to ensure PII is redacted.
[07:12] Max: we support configurable retention and automated PII redaction patterns; also you can forward raw or redacted logs to your S3 for eDiscovery.
[07:25] Marcus: competitor question - we evaluated doing this in-house on preemptible instances; main pushback was ops cost and burst handling.
[07:33] Samir: yes that's common - Redwood's value is unified runtime plus optimize tooling that shows the economics.
[07:40] Priya: pricing - can you give a quick sketch of numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated for our projected 3m tokens/day?
[07:48] Samir: rough sketch - hosted would be X per token (we'll send exact sheet); Dedicated amortized rate depends on commit level, roughly 40-60% cost savings at high sustained throughput in our examples; but depends on batchability and model mix.
[08:10] Jenna: i'll demo the Cost Breakdown view - it shows cost by route, model, and tags, and you can run 'what-if' scenarios toggling batching and quantized model to see projected monthly bill.
[08:30] Jenna: here's an export of the per-route cost table - sample columns: route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost, p95_latency, errors. (Export link: https://redwood.link/exports/aurora-cost-20260305.csv)
[08:55] Marcus: neat. can we restrict who sees cost vs who sees latency? role-based access?
[09:02] Max: yes RBAC is available - you can set read/write scopes on dashboards and exports; cost views can be limited to finance or admins.
[09:15] Priya: are there hooks for routing policy - say route A should prefer cheaper model unless p95 > 500ms?
[09:23] Jenna: yes policy engine supports rules: prefer model variant X for route tag 'low_cost', fallback to variant Y when latency crosses threshold, and route by geo or capacity. the console shows active policies and their last triggered time.
[09:45] Owen: can you do a short demo of the policy page?
[09:50] Jenna: (screen) create policy -> conditions -> actions. here's an example 'search-low-cost' policy. it's a little fiddly to set up but we provide templates.
[10:10] Marcus: perfect. for the POC we'll want a short checklist: benchmark with our traces, deploy a Dedicated or Hosted trial, run 1 week of live traffic and compare.
[10:22] Samir: agreed. jenna will run a sim, we'll size Dedicated options and share pricing; max will coordinate legal/contract.
[10:30] Leah: procurement needs sample MSA and data processing addendum.
[10:35] Samir: i'll include both in the follow-up.
[10:42] Marcus: any limitations on private deploy (VPC/on-prem) we should know about?
[10:46] Jenna: for Private we do a separate control plane and customer-managed networking; on-prem has extra setup time and stricter isolation - we can share the checklist.
[10:55] Owen: what's the expected time to launch a Dedicated pilot?
[10:58] Samir: once SOW signed, typical 2-4 weeks for Dedicated provisioning depending on region and capacity.
[11:10] Jenna: quick note - the console can surface 'regression alerts' if a model rollout increases cost or decreases quality on a set of eval prompts, helpful for canaries.
[11:25] Marcus: that sounds useful. ok real quick recap?
[11:30] Samir: recap: we will send pricing and contract (Samir), jenna sends benchmark spreadsheet and dashboard screenshots, samir and max to propose Dedicated sizing and POC plan, aurora to send traffic profile and route list. schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-03-16.
[11:50] Max: i'll schedule the kickoff and include legal contacts.
[12:00] Meeting end.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present - names sometimes spelled weirdly (e.g., 'Red Wood' instead of Redwood), timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts: Deck: https://redwood.link/decks/console-walkthrough.pdf, Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.link/benchmarks/aurora-03, Export CSV: https://redwood.link/exports/aurora-cost-20260305.csv
